source.author: lucan
source.text: Non me laetorum comitem rebusque secundis Accipis: in curas venio partemque laborum.
source.text_original: Non me laetorum comitem rebusque secundis / Accipis: in curas venio partemque laborum.
source.text_english: You do not receive me as a companion in happy times and favorable fortunes: I come to share your cares and part of your labors.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: contra effusa manus haerensque in pectore coniunx me quoque ait casus comitem quicumque propinquat accipies, nec fata traham natumque videbo te sine, sat caeli patiens, cum prima per altum vela dedit, potui quae tantum ferre dolorem.
reuse.text_original: contra effusa manus haerensque in pectore coniunx / 'me quoque' ait 'casus comitem quicumque propinquat / accipies, nec fata traham natumque videbo / te sine, sat caeli patiens, cum prima per altum / vela dedit, potui quae tantum ferre dolorem.
reuse.text_english: Against it, with hands outstretched and his wife clinging to his breast, he said: You too will accept me as companion in whatever fate draws near; I shall not drag out my destiny nor see my son without you. Patient enough of heaven as I am, when first she set sail over the deep, I was able to endure only so much grief.
